The shape

Nothing to fasten. Nothing to break.

The Japanese knot bag has two handles of different lengths. Slip the long one through the short one and the bag closes itself — tension does the work, so there is no clasp, no magnet and no zip to wear out.

Julia keeps that structure and puts it in evening cloth: heavy bridal satin, silver duchesse, floral brocade. Some are finished with a deep silk fringe. Each is cut, sewn and pressed by hand, and no two are made the same.

The making

Three things worth looking at closely.

The maker

Julia sews every one herself.

She started making these for a friend's wedding, when nothing in the shops matched the dress. The friend's guests asked where the bag came from, and it went from there.

Each bag is cut from a paper pattern on the kitchen table, sewn, turned and pressed by hand. Satin marks if you look at it wrong, so it is slow work, and there is only ever one of any cloth.

She answers her own messages — usually the same evening.

A knot is an honest closure. It either holds or it doesn't, and you can see which.Julia

Bespoke
